name.en-US: Sts. John de Brébeuf and Isaac Jogues
name.pt-BR: Santos João de Brébeuf e Isaac Jogues

prayerExcerpt.en-US: That the faith of Christians may be strengthened day by day.
prayerExcerpt.pt-BR: Que a fé dos cristãos se torne cada dia mais firme.

meta.face: Two clearly different men. Brébeuf (left): a tall, powerfully built man of about fifty-five with a large, long, strong-boned face — a high, bald dome of a forehead with a short fringe of grey hair at the sides, a big, straight, prominent nose, deep-set steady grey eyes under heavy brows, broad cheekbones and a strong jaw under a clipped salt-and-pepper beard and moustache, cut to a blunt point; a grave, manly, fatherly look. Jogues (right): a slighter man of about thirty-nine with a narrower, finer, oval face — dark-brown hair receding high from the forehead, gently arched brows, soft brown eyes lowered, a thin straight nose, a small mouth, and a short dark-brown pointed beard with a light moustache; a gentle, humble, prayerful look.
meta.basis: Parkman calls Brébeuf 'a tall, strong man, with features that seemed carved by Nature for a soldier', and his traditional portrait shows a bald crown and a grey pointed beard; Jogues follows Donald Guthrie McNab's 1895 portrait, a receding hairline, gentle lowered eyes and a short dark beard. Ages at their deaths (1649 and 1646).
